question: Who or what is the imperishable person (akṣara, called kūṭastha) of BhG 15.16, set beside the perishable (all beings) and below the highest person, and so what does it mean that the Lord is 'higher even than the imperishable' (15.18)?

sides.party: Śaṅkara, Gītābhāṣya on 15.16-18 (recalled, not checked against the bhāṣya, which is not available locally)
sides.position: The imperishable is the Lord's power of māyā, the seed from which the perishable arises, in which the impressions of the desires and actions of transmigrating beings rest; the highest person is distinct from both the perishable and this imperishable.

sides.party: Rāmānuja, Gītābhāṣya on 15.16-18 (recalled, not checked against the bhāṣya, which is not available locally)
sides.position: The perishable are the bound selves joined to non-conscious matter, called 'all beings'; the imperishable is the released self, free from connection with matter and so unchanging (kūṭastha); the Lord is other than both.
The perishable are all souls, whose bodies perish; the imperishable is Lakṣmī, whose body never perishes; the highest person is Viṣṇu, beyond both.
arguments: recorded in data/ as the Dvaita definition of cpt:ksara-aksara-purusottama (U15)

notes: The text's own statement: there are two puruṣas in the world, the perishable (all beings) and the imperishable, called the one standing firm (kūṭastha) (15.16); the highest puruṣa is another, called the supreme self, the imperishable lord who enters and sustains the three worlds (15.17); being beyond the perishable and higher even than the imperishable, the speaker is renowned as puruṣottama (15.18). The imperishable worshipped in 12.3 is also called kūṭastha (see dsp:bhagavad-gita-lord-or-unmanifest); the commentators do not all identify the two. The positions are recorded from recollection, not from the bhāṣyas (reserved for Wave 2), and must be checked before any upgrade. Proposed by extractor B; extractor A's link to the registry id dsp:saguna-nirguna at 15.18 is mapped here, and the saguṇa/nirguṇa reading of 15.16-18 is flagged for U50. Related: dsp:gita-primary-teaching (its Dvaita side rests on 15.16-18), cpt:three-purusas, cpt:ksara-aksara-purusottama. No reconciliation is attempted (extraction layer).

question: In what sense is the living being 'a portion of me' (mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ, BhG 15.7)?

sides.party: Śaṅkara, Gītābhāṣya on 15.7 (recalled, not checked against the bhāṣya, which is not available locally)
sides.position: A portion only as it were: as the sun's reflection in water, or the space enclosed by a pot, the individual appears as a part of the Lord through limiting adjuncts; when these are removed it is not other than him.
arguments: the images of the reflected sun and the pot-space (recalled)

sides.party: Rāmānuja, Gītābhāṣya on 15.7 and Śrībhāṣya on BS 2.3.43 (recalled, not checked against the bhāṣya, which is not available locally)
sides.position: A real and eternal part of the Lord, related to him as a mode or attribute to its substance; 'eternal' (sanātana) shows that the part and its distinctness are lasting.

sides.party: Madhva's school (school doctrine recalled by extractor B; Madhva's own comment on 15.7 not consulted; low confidence)
sides.position: A separated portion (vibhinnāṃśa), eternally distinct from and dependent on the Lord and like him only in part, as distinct from the Lord's own forms (svāṃśa).

notes: The text's own statement: 'a portion of me indeed (mamaiva aṃśaḥ), eternal, having become the living being in the world of the living, draws the senses with the mind as the sixth, which abide in prakṛti' (15.7); the verse says 'of me', not 'of brahman'. The commentators' positions are recorded from recollection, not from their texts (reserved for Wave 2), and must be checked before any upgrade. Proposed by extractor B; extractor A's link to the registry id dsp:souls-one-or-distinct at 15.7 is mapped here. Related: dsp:aupadhika-vs-svabhavika-bhedabheda (the Bhedābheda schools' accounts of the soul as part, on BS 2.3.43), dsp:souls-one-or-distinct (registry, U50), cpt:jiva-as-part-of-brahman. No reconciliation is attempted (extraction layer).

question: When the Lord says 'know me also as the knower of the field (kṣetrajña) in all fields' (BhG 13.3 in this edition; 13.2 in the 700-verse numbering) and names the highest puruṣa in the body the great lord and the supreme self (13.23; 13.22 in the 700-verse numbering), is the knower of the field in each body the Lord himself, or is the Lord the self of the knowers, distinct from them?

sides.party: Śaṅkara, Gītābhāṣya on 13.2 in the 700-verse numbering (recalled, not checked against the bhāṣya, which is not available locally)
sides.position: The knower of the field in all bodies is the Lord himself, free of all adjuncts; its appearance as a transmigrating agent and experiencer belongs to the field and is due to ignorance (avidyā); knowing this identity is the knowledge the verse speaks of.
arguments: 'know me also (api)': the Lord is identified with the kṣetrajña named in 13.2 (recalled)
13.23 names the highest puruṣa in this body the supreme self (paramātman) (recalled)

sides.party: Rāmānuja, Gītābhāṣya on 13.2 in the 700-verse numbering (recalled, not checked against the bhāṣya, which is not available locally)
sides.position: The Lord is the self (ātman) of all the knowers of the field, who with their bodies are his body; 'kṣetrajña' in 'know me also as the kṣetrajña' denotes the Lord as having them for his body, so they are one with him as body with self while remaining distinct individual selves.
arguments: co-reference (sāmānādhikaraṇya) of words denoting the body with the self that has it (recalled)

sides.party: Madhva's school (recalled from the U05 skeleton note and extractor A's note; low confidence; Madhva's comment not consulted)
sides.position: The Lord is the independent knower in all fields, eternally distinct from the dependent individual knowers whom he controls.

notes: The text's own statements: the body is the field and its knower the kṣetrajña (13.2); the Lord is 'also' to be known as the kṣetrajña in all fields (13.3); the highest puruṣa in this body is onlooker, consenter, supporter, experiencer, great lord, and is called the supreme self (13.23); every being arises from the union of field and knower (13.27). The commentators' positions are recorded from the extractors' and the merger's recollection of the bhāṣyas, not from their texts (the Sanskrit commentaries of the gita/gita corpus are reserved for Wave 2); every side must be checked against src:gita-bhasya-sankara, src:gita-bhasya-ramanuja and src:gita-bhasya-madhva before any upgrade. Proposed by extractor B; extractor A's links to the registry id dsp:souls-one-or-distinct (U50, not yet in data/) at 13.3 and 13.23 are mapped here; the Dvaita side is added from the U05 skeleton teaching 13.1-2 (700-verse numbering) and A's note.
